RAMALLAH, occupied West Bank--In the aftermath of Friday's killings in the
village of Tal, hundreds of armed Israeli settlers and soldiers launched a
campaign of terror targeting Palestinian towns and villages across the
occupied West Bank, with reports of home raids, shootings, assaults, mass
detentions, and demolitions of property--including residential buildings,
mosques, cars, agricultural equipment, and farmland.

It began when armed settlers raided Tal, which is southwest of Nablus city in
the northern West Bank, at around 7 a.m. local time and opened fire. They were
confronted by Palestinian residents of the village who were attempting to
protect their homes and land. Just a week earlier, armed settlers had raided
Tal and set fire to a Palestinian home. The family managed to escape before
the house was consumed by flames.

During Friday's attack, one of the Palestinian residents, Farouq Ramadan, a
father of five, managed to seize the machine gun of an Israeli settler in a
moment captured on camera. Ramadan then shot one of the settlers. Ramadan, and
three of his cousins-- brothers Jawad and Ibrahim Ramadan, and their cousin
Imran--were then shot dead by settlers and soldiers, while two settlers were
killed.

"This was self-defense. Farouq was defending himself, his uncle and his
cousins. Farouq is well-known in our village--he has never gone out to
confront the occupation and its forces and settlers. Had the settlers not been
close to his sister's home in the village he would not have gone out," Firas
al-Saifi, a local Palestinian journalist from Tal, told Drop Site. "The
situation is that they raid Palestinian villages and homes and point their
guns at residents, and expect them to be killed in silence."

Four others were shot and wounded at the scene by settler and soldier fire,
including Orwa Ramadan, the brother of Jawad and Ibrahim, who was shot in the
shoulder. Shortly after the attack, Israeli soldiers abducted Orwa from his
hospital bed at the Nablus Specialty Hospital, where he was transferred for
treatment. He remains detained along with another one of his brothers, Majd
Ramadan, who was at work and uninvolved during the attack.

The arrests came amid a sweeping campaign of mass detentions across the West
Bank by Israeli occupation forces, with more than 100 Palestinians taken into
custody and interrogated, according to local officials. More than 20 remain in
custody as of Monday.

Israeli forces also raided Ramadan's home, taking measurements in preparation
for the planned demolition of his family home and that of his parents, who
live on the lower floor of the same building. Armed settlers, accompanied by
the Israeli military, established a new illegal outpost--installing caravans
after uprooting hundreds of Palestinian-owned olive trees in the area.

It is one of at least six new colonial outposts reported on occupied
Palestinian land as Israeli settlers take advantage of the mass crackdown they
incited, in addition to the expansion of existing outposts over the past few
days alone with the support of the Israeli army. Other outposts established by
Israeli settlers over the weekend in Palestinian villages include in Umm Safa
and Sinjil in the Ramallah governorate; in Deir Ballut in the Salfit
governorate; Asira al-Shamaliya in the Nablus governorate and another existing
one in Nablus, Madama, that is being expanded.

**[MORE: Video obtained by Drop Site of the new settler outpost at
Tal](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2081050132355641722)**

## **Expanding Attacks and Colonization**

Once the news of the two killed Israelis emerged on Friday, hundreds more
settlers attacked at least 30 different villages and locations between Friday
and midday on Monday. The Israeli army not only supported the settlers but
launched its own military raids.

Dozens of Palestinians were wounded, including many through live ammunition,
rubber-coated bullets, rocks, pepper-spray, and physical assaults. At least
seven homes, two mosques, a quarry, many cars, and farmlands were set on fire
and burned, while many other properties faced arson attempts but were blocked
by residents.

Reports of attacks came from numerous villages, including Tal, Surra, Qusra,
Urif, Madama, Asira al-Qibliya, Burin, Iraq Burin, Qabalan, Jalud, Qaryut,
Aqraba, Beita, Lubban al-Sharqiya, Wadi al-Sha'ir, Khirbat Tana al-Fawqa, Beit
Furik, As-Sawiya, Tilfeet, and Huwwara in the Nablus district; Jit, Fara'ta,
and Immatin in the Qalqilya district; Kur in the Tulkarem district; Sinjil,
Beitillu, and Ein Samiya in the Ramallah and al-Bireh district; Surif in the
Hebron district; and al-Maniya in the Bethlehem district.

Compounding the attacks, the Israeli army imposed a suffocating lockdown on
Palestinian cities and severed movement between towns and villages,
effectively trapping residents as the attacks were underway. Because of
blocked access to essential services, according to local medics, there have
been at least four cases of Palestinian women being forced to give birth at
military closures and checkpoints over the weekend, with ambulances blocked
from evacuating them. On Monday, one woman tragically delivered a stillborn
after enduring severe bleeding due to the closures by the Israeli army.
Soldiers held the ambulance for more than 30 minutes at Nablus, searched the
woman despite her condition, and ordered the crew to switch off the vehicle's
engine, shutting down its medical equipment. The woman survived after reaching
hospital, but lost her baby.

Bashar Qaryouti, a volunteer medic and activist from the village of Qaryout
south of Nablus city, explained that the current period marks a clear shift.
"We used to be afraid of the night--we called the settlers 'bats' because they
used to carry out their attacks under the cover of darkness. Now, they commit
all their crimes in broad daylight without a care in the world," Qaryouti told
Drop Site.

Following the killings, Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who is also
in charge of the building of illegal colonies in the occupied West Bank,
[called for](https://www.reuters.com/world/one-killed-two-injured-shooting-
incident-west-bank-2026-07-24/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) the destruction of
Palestinian villages and the transfer of their residents, and demanded the
expansion of Israeli colonies. A [similar
statement](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20260724-four-palestinians-
and-one-israeli-killed-in-occupied-west-bank-shooting) was made by Israeli
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz, who
announced a series of measures, among them the building of new colonies.

While most settler attacks in recent years have focused on Palestinians living
in Area C--the area comprising roughly 60 percent of the occupied West Bank
and excluding the built-up areas of Palestinian cities and villages--settler
violence is now increasingly moving into Areas A and B, where the majority of
Palestinian villages are located.

"We are in a new stage. The settlers and soldiers have emptied about 99
percent of Area C through their attacks and by forcing residents out, and now
the settlers are moving into the villages and attacking them. They have begun
taking over homes on the edges of villages and launching attacks deep inside
our towns," Qaryouti said.

One of the new outposts is in Deir Istya, a historic Palestinian town in the
Salfit governorate in the northern West Bank. "The place where they
established [one of the new outposts] is the only remaining open space
available for the people of Deir Istya to expand their construction in the
future. The area they have taken control of covers 44 dunams (around 10
acres)," Izzat Mansour, the mayor of Deir Istya, told Drop Site on Monday.
"They set up tents there last night, and since three o'clock this morning
Israeli army forces have been present there. All the surrounding areas of Deir
Istya are already enclosed by settlers."

"We see that what happened to our people in 1948 is now being repeated in the
West Bank," Mansour added, referring to the mass expulsion of 750,000
Palestinians from their homes by Zionist militias in what is known as the
Nakba, Arabic for 'catastrophe.' "There is continuous and systematic daily
harassment from different directions by settlers. We are using every means
available to us to continue living on these lands, to resist displacement, and
to prevent them from gaining control over these areas and imposing a new
reality."

Routine attacks by Israeli settlers and soldiers on Palestinians in the West
Bank have been taking place for decades, but over the last few years,
particularly since the genocide in Gaza began in 2023, they have significantly
increased and become more organized. The Israeli military also increasingly
shows up to support the settlers' actions.

Sinjil, a Palestinian village northeast of Ramallah, was close to one of the
new outposts established this weekend. "Before the events of Tal--two or three
days before--Sinjil was attacked by dozens of armed settlers. They fired live
ammunition directly at people…The settlers have gone far beyond all limits.
Their attacks have escalated to the point where they enter people's homes,
vandalize shops, vandalize houses. These are systematic attacks. They steal
money--anything they can get their hands on," Mohammad Ghafry, a resident of
Sinjil. "Since the events in Tal, they have tightened the closure of Sinjil.
All of the town's entrances have been completely sealed off."

"In addition to that, they established a new settlement outpost in the eastern
plain," Ghafry added. "These lands belong to al-Mazra'a al-Sharqiya, not
Sinjil, but the outpost is located at Sinjil's eastern entrance. The settlers
in this outpost have effectively become like the army's eyes."

Before the attacks on Tal, more than 80 Palestinians had already been killed
by Israeli soldiers and settlers in the occupied West Bank so far in 2026,
according to the Palestinian Health Ministry

The coordination between armed settlers and Israeli occupation forces is
painfully clear, Qaryouti said. "They have worked together for a long time,
but now they do it openly."

"Both the occupation authorities and the settlers are deliberately pushing
Palestinians towards an explosion because it serves their broader settlement
plan."
